discussion_comments.comment_body: This one doesn't hold. Without `-m`, `git read-tree <tree1> <tree2>` reads both trees into stage 0; it only fails if they share a path, and a checkpoint's tracked tree and its untracked-files parent never do. Repro on git 2.43: read-tree of a tree with `a.ts` and a tree with `new.ts` gives `100644 ... 0 a.ts` and `100644 ... 0 new.ts`, and `write-tree` succeeds. The path is also covered by `sidecar/session-changes.test.ts`, whose checkpoints carry an untracked third parent (including an agent-created `new.ts`), and by a manual run where agent-created untracked files showed up in Last turn and Session.

Fixed in `1544b995b`. `suggestion()` in `candidates.ts` now clips `prompt` to `PROMPT_MAX_CHARS` and `why` to `WHY_MAX_CHARS` before it hashes the id, so rule, model and turn rows all stay inside the published bounds. Text within the limits is unchanged, so the `host-rules.json` parity fixtures keep their ids. `contracts.test.ts` builds rows from a long task title, a status headline and a failing check list, and validates the set and push against `NextTurnSet` and `NextTurnTrayPush`.

Fixed in 2c1a7f7d7: normalization now recurses into `items` (object and tuple forms) and into `anyOf`/`oneOf`/`allOf` branches before the object-likeness gate, so nested uppercase types lowercase at every depth. Covered by the new "normalizes nested array items and combinator branches" test.

discussion_comments.comment_body:
The 32k floor is intentional following review feedback: applying 30% directly lowered existing output allowances and could cause more truncation and retries.
Compared with main, an 8k model still receives an 8k cap, and a 64k model still receives 32k. Only sufficiently large models receive an increase. For example, 128k → 38,400. The existing model and context clamps remain in place.
The PR description still described the earlier proportional reduction; I’ve corrected it. Using the fraction directly would reintroduce the issue identified in the earlier review, so I believe this P1 can be closed.
